title: Axis Bank Profit Jumps 38 Percent as Provisions Halve and Loans Grow
excerpt: Standalone net profit rose to Rs 7,003 crore in Q2 FY27 as provisions fell 52 percent and advances grew 23 percent, though margin slipped to 3.36 percent and profit trailed consensus.
body:
• Axis Bank reported standalone net profit of Rs 7,003 crore for the September quarter (Q2 FY27), up 38 percent from Rs 5,090 crore a year earlier, according to its exchange filing.
  • The jump was driven mainly by provisions falling 52 percent to Rs 1,694 crore — the year-ago quarter carried a one-time Rs 1,231 crore standard asset provision — while net interest income rose 12 percent to Rs 15,371 crore.
  • Advances grew 23 percent year on year to Rs 13.74 lakh crore and deposits 21 percent to Rs 14.52 lakh crore; gross NPA improved to 1.16 percent from 1.46 percent.
  • For investors: profit was slightly below consensus estimates near Rs 7,124 crore and down about 1.6 percent from the June quarter, and net interest margin slipped to 3.36 percent — margin, not the headline growth rate, is the number to watch when the stock opens Monday.

Axis Bank, India's third-largest private sector lender by assets, reported a 38 percent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, supported by strong loan growth, higher net interest income and improving asset quality, according to The Economic Times and the bank's exchange filing. Consolidated net profit was Rs 7,705 crore.

The headline growth rate needs context. Profit was about 1.6 percent lower than the Rs 7,114 crore earned in the June quarter, and it came in slightly below consensus estimates. The year-ago comparison is also flattered by a one-time charge: the September 2025 quarter included a one-time standard asset provision of Rs 1,231 crore, which depressed the base against which this year's 38 percent rise is measured.

Provisions Did the Heavy Lifting

Provisions and contingencies fell to Rs 1,694 crore from Rs 3,547 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, a decline of 52 percent, according to the bank's earnings release and investor presentation filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday. Operating profit before provisions rose more modestly, to Rs 11,083 crore from Rs 10,413 crore a year earlier.

Asset quality improved on every measure the bank highlighted. Gross non-performing assets declined to 1.16 percent from 1.46 percent a year earlier, and net NPAs improved to 0.35 percent from 0.44 percent. Fresh loan slippages fell to Rs 4,762 crore from Rs 5,696 crore in the year-ago quarter, and the annualised net credit cost declined to 0.45 percent, down 28 basis points year on year. The provision coverage ratio stood at 70 percent.

Loan and Deposit Growth

Net interest income rose 12 percent year on year and 5 percent sequentially to Rs 15,371 crore. Net interest margin stood at 3.36 percent; excluding the impact of foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposit mobilisation, the margin was 3.47 percent, compared with 3.46 percent in the preceding quarter. The bank reported raising Rs 1.018 lakh crore in FCNR-B deposits during the period, and the month-end CASA ratio stood at 36 percent.

The bank's net advances rose 23 percent year on year to Rs 13.74 lakh crore, while total deposits increased 21 percent to Rs 14.52 lakh crore. Corporate loans rose 34 percent, outpacing retail loan growth of 16 percent, while small and medium enterprise loans increased 25 percent. Fee income rose 6 percent to Rs 6,381 crore, with granular fees accounting for 90 percent of the total. The cost-to-assets ratio declined to 2.14 percent, down 24 basis points year on year.

"As customer expectations continue to evolve, our focus remains on building a franchise that combines innovation, trust and execution at scale."

— Amitabh Chaudhry, Managing Director and CEO, Axis Bank

Subsidiaries and Capital

The bank's domestic subsidiaries delivered a combined profit after tax of Rs 1,210 crore for the first half of FY27, up 29 percent year on year. Axis Finance reported a 42 percent increase in first-half profit, while Axis Asset Management Company's profit grew 36 percent. Capital adequacy remained at 16.27 percent, and the bank reported an average liquidity coverage ratio of about 119 percent for the quarter, according to its results summary. Axis also held about 38 percent market share in UPI payer payment service provider volume and a 25.7 percent share in merchant-acquiring terminals.

What Investors Will Watch

Axis was the first of India's large private lenders to report for the quarter, ahead of HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, making its numbers an early read on sector loan growth and deposit costs. The questions for the coming quarters are whether credit growth near 23 percent can be sustained without further margin compression, whether the FCNR-B deposit base reprices expensively, and whether slippages stay at this quarter's lower level. The balance sheet is cleaner than a year ago; the earnings debate is now about margins, not asset quality.
